title: Facets Of Contact Geometry
notes: Open the lecture by treating Chapter 1 as a map rather than as a list of definitions. The first invariant is local non-integrability, but the point of the chapter is that the same invariant reappears in line elements, transformations of differential equations, mechanics, geodesics, wavefronts, contact tests, and topology.

title: Hyperplane Fields Before Contact
notes: Start from the ordinary language of distributions. A coorientable hyperplane field can be written as the kernel of a global one-form, so the geometry can be tested by differential forms. Contrast this with Frobenius integrability: if alpha wedge d alpha vanishes, the planes fit together into leaves; contact geometry asks for the opposite local behavior.

title: Maximal Non-Integrability
notes: Make the definition feel like a volume test. The one-form alpha picks the hyperplane field, while d alpha measures how the planes rotate. Requiring alpha wedge d alpha to the n to be nowhere zero says that the rotation fills every remaining direction and cannot be removed by rescaling the defining form.

title: The Standard Model
notes: Use the local figure as a reading exercise. The blue direction is partial x, while the tilted direction is partial y minus x partial z. At x equals zero the tilt disappears, and on either side it leans in opposite vertical directions. The bracket records the same shear algebraically by producing a direction outside the plane field.

title: Reeb Direction And Lambda Check
notes: Separate the contact structure from the chosen contact form. For a fixed form, the Reeb vector is the unique direction killed by d alpha and normalized by alpha. In the lambda family, the saved check says that the volume coefficient equals lambda: zero is integrable failure, nonzero values are contact, and the standard Reeb direction is partial z.

title: Contact Elements
notes: Now explain why the name contact geometry is historically natural. A contact element is first-order tangent hyperplane data at a base point. Projectivized cotangent space records those hyperplanes up to scale, and the kernel of the Liouville one-form descends to a canonical hyperplane field on this bundle without choosing coordinates on the base.

title: ODEs And Contact Transformations
notes: Translate the bundle picture into the classical line-element picture. A graph z of x lifts to the curve of its position and slope, and the equation dz minus p dx equals zero is exactly the tangency condition. A contact transformation preserves this condition up to a nowhere-zero scale, so it carries solution lifts to solution lifts.

title: Projective Polarity
notes: Use the conic picture to show that contact geometry is not only analytic. A conic defines a polarity, sending a point to its polar line and a line to its pole. The induced map on contact elements reverses the base and fibre roles while preserving incidence, which is the projective version of preserving contact data.

title: Symplectic Linear Algebra Bridge
notes: Pause on the linear algebra because it is the bridge between contact and symplectic geometry. The symplectic orthogonal has the dimension formula shown on the slide. On each contact plane, d alpha is nondegenerate, so contact geometry contains a symplectic vector space at every point, one dimension below the ambient tangent space.

title: Classical Mechanics
notes: Present mechanics as the cotangent-bundle facet of the same story. The Liouville form is the canonical one-form on phase space, its exterior derivative is symplectic, and a Hamiltonian determines a vector field by contraction with omega. The skew-symmetry then forces dH of X_H to vanish, which is the coordinate-free statement of energy preservation.

title: Contact Type And Hopf Reeb Flow
notes: Connect the mechanics slide to a contact hypersurface. On a contact-type level set, the restricted Liouville form becomes a contact form, and the Reeb dynamics agree with Hamiltonian dynamics up to reparametrization. The displayed standard sphere form explains the factor of two in the Hopf Reeb field.

title: Cogeodesic Reeb Flow
notes: Use the theorem as a compression of several languages. The metric identifies tangent and cotangent bundles by Psi. Under that identification, the geodesic vector field on the unit tangent bundle becomes the Reeb vector field of the Liouville contact form on the unit cotangent bundle. This is why geodesic propagation is a contact phenomenon.

title: Contact Vector Fields
notes: Distinguish strict preservation of a form from preservation of its kernel. If the Lie derivative of alpha is zero, the flow preserves the chosen measuring form. If the Lie derivative is mu times alpha, the form may rescale but its kernel is unchanged. This distinction will matter whenever the geometry is the plane field rather than a selected alpha.

title: Legendrian Fronts And Huygens
notes: Read the wavefront diagram through contact elements. A front is the visible projection; the Legendrian lift stores the missing tangent hyperplane or coorientation. Huygens propagation evolves those contact elements by the cogeodesic Reeb flow, and the next front is reconstructed as the envelope of the propagated tangent data.

title: Order Of Contact
notes: Return to the original non-integrability test, now without relying on the exterior derivative as the first language. Locally, a plane field can be written as the kernel of dz plus a dx plus b dy. The inequality a_y at zero not equal to b_x at zero is exactly the first-order obstruction to finding a surface with second-order contact.

title: Topology Applications
notes: Keep this slide as a dependency map, not as a proof. The chapter points forward to two topology stories. For Cerf's theorem, classification and rigidity of contact structures on the three-sphere enter the extension problem. For Property P, contact and symplectic filling ideas are part of the route to the theorem about non-trivial knot surgeries.

title: Recap Checks
notes: Close by asking students to connect formulas to inspections. The contact condition, Reeb normalization, line-element form, Liouville form, Hamiltonian equation, cogeodesic theorem, and order-of-contact test should now look like facets of one object. The final prompts make them name which object is preserved and which invariant verifies the claim.
